newsitem.title: NORWAY: Scientists stumped in McDonald's McLaks mystery.
newsitem.headline: Scientists stumped in McDonald's McLaks mystery.

text.p: Norwegian scientists were mystified on Friday by an apparent food poisoning outbreak that hospitalised four people and forced U.S. fast-food giant McDonald's Corp to withdraw its McLaks salmon burgers in Norway.
John Kristian Taerud, head of the Municipal Food Control Authority in Stroemmen, near Oslo, said analysis of several samples of McLaks had failed to uncover the source of the poisoning.
He said his team would confer with the national Norwegian Food Control Authority and researchers at the University of Oslo next week.

"We will discuss what steps we should take next. We know from blood controls that these people were sick from a form of poisoning, but we have not been able to discover what it was," Taerud told Reuters.

McDonald's withdrew salmon burgers from all 36 branches in Norway after two customers and two employees apparently became ill on Sunday after eating McLaks meals at a restaurant in Loerenskog outside Oslo.
The four were taken to hospital complaining of paralysis in the mouth, burning sensations, trembling, itching and rashes. All four have since been released.

Taerud said tests to date had concentrated on detecting the biological amines histamine, cadaverine and putricine, which are produced when bacteria absorb the amino acid histidine, a natural substance found in most fish.
The amines at certain levels in the body cause symptoms similar to those described by the four patients, he said.

Agnete Samdahl, spokeswoman for McDonald's in Norway, said the company had withdrawn the product as a precaution until the situation had been clarified, but it continued to have confidence in Norwegian salmon.
"We really believe in this product and we have great faith in Norwegian salmon," Samdahl said.
